name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1st August 2024 and completed my full 60-day notice period till 30th September 2024. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My August salary was delayed, and my September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

case_dossier.case_title: Unpaid Salary and Withholding of Relieving Letter
case_dossier.summary: A frontend developer resigned after completing a 60‑day notice period but has not received his September salary, leave encashment of Rs 1,65,000 and his August salary. The employer is also refusing to issue the relieving and experience letters, jeopardising his new job.

September salary + 15 days encashable leave (Rs 1,65,000) not paid

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You have a clear legal right to receive all wages that are due to you, including your August salary, September salary and the payment for your encashed leave. Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 and the relevant State Shops & Establishments Act, an employer must pay wages within 7‑10 days of the wage period and must settle any full‑and‑final dues within 30 days of your last working day. Withholding your relieving and experience letters after you have served the full notice period is also unlawful – the Delhi High Court in Milan Sharma v. State held that such a refusal violates your constitutional right to livelihood. Because the employer has not paid you and is keeping your documents hostage, you can demand payment and the letters as a civil matter, without needing to involve the criminal courts.

governing_laws.relevance: Mandates timely payment of wages and bars unauthorized deductions.

governing_laws.act_name: State Shops & Commercial Establishments Act (Full & Final Rules)
governing_laws.relevance: Requires processing of full‑and‑final dues and issuance of relieving/experience letters within 30 days of termination.

governing_laws.act_name: Milan Sharma v. State (Delhi High Court)
governing_laws.relevance: Precedent that withholding relieving letters infringes the employee’s right to livelihood.

action_options.title: Send Formal Legal Notice to Employer
action_options.details: Draft a concise notice stating: (a) amount of unpaid salary (August & September) and leave encashment, (b) demand for interest as per Section 15, (c) request for immediate issuance of relieving and experience letters, (d) a deadline of 15 days to comply. Attach copies of appointment letter, resignation acceptance, asset clearance form, and any email proof of salary delay. Send by registered post (Speed Post) and email, keeping a copy for your records.

action_options.title: File Complaint with District Labor Commissioner / Labor Inspector
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees; nominal filing fee (if any) up to Rs. 500
action_options.details: Visit the Labour Department website of your state (e.g., labour.gov.in) and use the e‑complaint portal, or go in person to the District Labour Commissioner’s office. Submit the legal notice copy, employment documents, and a written statement of unpaid wages and withheld letters. The Commissioner can issue a direction for payment, interest, and release of documents, and may impose penalties on the employer.

action_options.title: Approach the Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal (or Consumer Forum if amount < Rs. 20 Lakhs)
action_options.timeline: 60‑90 days after filing the labour‑commissioner complaint
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal court fees (around Rs. 500‑1,000) plus modest lawyer’s fee if you choose representation
action_options.details: If the employer still does not comply, file a civil suit for recovery of wages and damages under the Payment of Wages Act before the appropriate Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal. You may also claim compensation for mental harassment. The suit can be filed by you personally; a lawyer is not mandatory but can help with drafting the plaint.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can represent yourself for the legal notice, the labour‑commissioner complaint, and even the labour‑court filing. A lawyer becomes useful if the employer contests the claim, files a counter‑claim, or if you need assistance in drafting a detailed plaint. Consumer Forums and Labour Courts allow self‑representation, so you may proceed without an advocate until the matter becomes contested.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekhiye, hum sab policy aur internal audit ke hisaab se hi kaam karte hain. Aapka resignation letter aur clearance form abhi tak HR ke paas final verification ke liye pending hai, isliye settlement process thoda delay ho raha hai. Company ke terms ke mutabik final dues ko clear karne ka samay 15 din ka hota hai, aur relieving letter tabhi issue hoti hai jab sab documents sign off ho jaye. Hum aapko guarantee dete hain ki aapka pending salary aur leave encashment ko hum agle 7 din ke andar process kar denge, lekin aapko bhi apne taraf se sab required paperwork turant submit karna hoga. Agar aapke paas koi specific grievance form ya legal notice hai, to please HR ko forward kar dein, tabhi hum aage badh sakte hain.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: Aapne sahi tarah se employment law ka reference diya, deadline set ki aur Labour Commissioner ko involve karne ki baat ki, jo aapki position ko majboot banata hai.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Abhi tak aapne apni resignation ki exact date, HR ko diye gaye clearance form ka reference, aur Payment of Wages Act ke specific clause (Section 15) ka zikr nahi kiya. In facts ko include karne se aapka case aur bhi damdaar hoga.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Mujhe mere resignation ki date (15 July 2024) aur HR ko diye gaye clearance form ka reference dekh kar turant settlement aur relieving letter issue karne ka notice dijiye, warna main Section 15, Payment of Wages Act ke tehat legal action lunga.
